deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is historical and critical prose, and it is a draft of part of the introductory history (end of §3) of Riemann's Habilitationsschrift 'Über die Darstellbarkeit einer Function durch eine trigonometrische Reihe' (written 1853/54, published posthumously by Dedekind in 1867, Abh. Ges. Wiss. Göttingen 13). The published text agrees with this draft almost word for word.

The argument, step by step:
(1) The page opens mid-sentence ('...[in dieser Be]ziehung hat die Behandlung derselben ein unmittelbares Interesse'). This continues the preceding claim that functions not covered by Dirichlet's conditions may occur in physics. So the treatment of such functions is of direct interest.
(2) Fourier series are no longer confined to physics. They have been applied with success in pure mathematics, namely number theory. This alludes to Dirichlet's work of 1837-1840: primes in arithmetic progressions, Gauss sums, class-number formulas. Riemann argues that precisely the functions whose representability Dirichlet did not examine seem important there. In the draft, 'durch die Fourier'sche Reihe' is struck and 'durch eine trigonometrische [Reihe]' is inserted.
(3) At the end of his 1829 Crelle paper, Dirichlet promised to return to the excluded cases (functions with infinitely many discontinuities or maxima and minima). That promise was still unfulfilled.
(4) The papers of Dirksen and Bessel on cosine and sine series do not supply this completion. They are inferior to Dirichlet's in rigour and generality.
- Dirksen (Abh. Berlin. Akad., 1829) was almost simultaneous with Dirichlet and evidently written without knowledge of his paper. Dirksen takes a correct general route but has inaccuracies. In one special case he obtains a wrong value for the sum of the series. In a side argument he relies on a series expansion that is possible only in special cases. Hence his proof is complete only for functions with everywhere finite first derivative.
- Bessel (Astron. Nachr. 16, 1839) tried to simplify Dirichlet's proof. His changes bring no essential simplification in the reasoning. At most they dress the proof in more familiar notions, while its rigour and generality suffer considerably.

No derivation, formula or computation appears on the page, so there is nothing to reconstruct mathematically.
errors: No mathematical errors, since the page has no mathematics.
The historical judgements are Riemann's own. They match the published Habilitationsschrift and the standard historiography of Dirksen's and Bessel's papers.

The draft wording differs slightly from the 1867 printed text: 'seine Änderungen' vs printed 'die Aenderungen', and the duplicated 'gerade', which is resolved in print as 'gerade hier scheinen diejenigen'.

results.what: Historical assessment of Dirichlet (1829), Dirksen (1829) and Bessel (1839) on the convergence of Fourier series. It notes Dirichlet's unfulfilled promise to treat the general case and the relevance of non-Dirichlet functions to number theory.
results.modern_name: History of Fourier series convergence (Dirichlet conditions); introduction to Riemann's Habilitationsschrift

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a draft of a passage that appears nearly verbatim in Riemann's published Habilitationsschrift on trigonometric series. It is purely historical prose with no new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: Line 4-5: the transcription 'gerade hier scheinen gerade diejenigen' has a duplicated 'gerade'. In the manuscript one occurrence appears to be struck or overwritten. The printed text reads 'und gerade hier scheinen diejenigen Functionen'.
The pencil interlinear insertion after 'Darstellbarkeit durch' reads 'eine trigonometrische', replacing the struck 'die Fourier'sche'. The intended reading is 'durch eine trigonometrische Reihe'.
'leisten[?]' is correct: 'leisten diese Ergänzung nicht', the word being written heavily or overwritten.
The struck fragment after 'in einem speciellen Falle' is unclear (perhaps 'er fast'). It is deleted and not in the printed text.
'Aber seine Änderungen {+in diesem Beweise+}': the insertion is an interlinear addition above 'Änderungen'. The printed version reads 'Aber die Aenderungen in diesem Beweise'.

The first line begins mid-word: '[Be]ziehung', continuing 'In dieser Beziehung' from a preceding page that is not the transcribed 'previous page' (which belongs to a later section of the same work, the n! example of §13).
